name: Red Mountain (Hendrickson Construction), Aspen CO
type: Luxury mountain residence, three stories of glass between sandstone piers under deep cedar soffits
location: Red Mountain, Aspen, Colorado (exact address not published)
summary: A house built by Hendrickson Construction and published as "Red Mountain" in its project gallery. The builder publishes photos and a one-line description only: no architect, no floor area, no plans. Every dimension below was read from the builder's dusk hero photo by an earlier build, or is an estimate. This is not the CCY Architects concrete house of the same name.

sources.title: Red Mountain from the outside (gallery image 01, dusk, oblique from the front right at about eye level)

images.caption: Hero photo: the house at dusk from the front right (the only exterior view the massing is read from)

location.label: Location
location.quote: "Red Mountain illustrates Hendrickson Construction's expertise in luxury mountain homes, combining architectural innovation with breathtaking Aspen views."

stories.label: Stories above grade
stories.derivation: Read from the hero photo (earlier reading): three bands of floor-to-ceiling bronze-framed glass, each capped by a slab fascia.

level1.label: Level 1 footprint (main block)
level1.derivation: Read from the hero photo (earlier reading): long front facade ~80-100 ft (92 ft used), short near-right facade ~45-55 ft (52 ft used). x runs along the front, z is depth, the front faces +z.

wing.label: Low wing at the far left (one level)
wing.derivation: Read from the hero photo (earlier reading): a one-storey glazed wing left of the main block with a railed roof deck. Its depth (38 ft) is not visible and follows the earlier build.

level2.label: Level 2 footprint (set back)
level2.derivation: Read from the hero photo (earlier reading): the second floor steps back behind a balcony 8-10 ft deep on the front and 6-7 ft on the near side.

level3.label: Level 3 footprint (set back again)
level3.derivation: Read from the hero photo (earlier reading): the top floor steps back again behind the level-3 balcony.

floorToFloor.label: Floor-to-floor heights, levels 1 / 2 / 3
floorToFloor.derivation: Read from the hero photo (earlier reading): floor-to-floor 11-13 ft and 36-44 ft to the roof. Slab tops at 12.2 and 24.6 ft and the roof base at 35.1 ft give 12.2, 12.4 and 10.5 ft.

slab1.label: Level-2 balcony slab (cantilevered): extent; top and thickness
slab1.derivation: Read from the hero photo (earlier reading): each upper level is a cantilevered slab 6-9 ft deep wrapping the front and near side; the fascia reads about a foot deep.

wingDeck.label: Wing roof deck slab: extent; top and thickness
wingDeck.derivation: Read from the hero photo (earlier reading): the wing's flat roof is a deck with a glass rail on its front edge. It stops where the level-2 balcony slab begins.

slab2.label: Level-3 balcony slab: extent; top and thickness
slab2.derivation: Read from the hero photo (earlier reading): the second cantilevered slab, with a deep cedar soffit underneath.

roof.label: Roof slab: extent; base and thickness
roof.derivation: Read from the hero photo (earlier reading): a big low-slope (nearly flat) roof with 8-12 ft cedar soffits and a dark bronze fascia. It is modelled as flat.

chimney1.label: Chimney 1: size, position, top
chimney1.derivation: Read from the hero photo (earlier reading): two stone chimneys rise above the roof; the right-hand one is the taller.

chimney2.label: Chimney 2: size, position, top
chimney2.derivation: Read from the hero photo (earlier reading): the left-hand chimney, smaller, about one course above the roof.

frontPiersL1.label: Level 1 front piers (offset from the wing's left corner, width)
frontPiersL1.derivation: Read from the hero photo (earlier reading): wing piers [0,5] and [13,4] from x -72; main-block piers [0,5], [19,5], [41,6], [62,5], [86,6] from x -46, here measured from x -72. Glass bays fill the gaps.

sidePiersL1.label: Level 1 near-side piers (offset from the front corner, width)
sidePiersL1.derivation: Read from the hero photo (earlier reading): the near-right facade shows full-height glass and two piers.

frontPiersL2.label: Level 2 front piers
frontPiersL2.derivation: Read from the hero photo (earlier reading), measured from x -44.

sidePiersL2.label: Level 2 near-side piers
sidePiersL2.derivation: Read from the hero photo (earlier reading), measured from the front corner (z 18).

frontPiersL3.label: Level 3 front piers
frontPiersL3.derivation: Read from the hero photo (earlier reading), measured from x -40.

sidePiersL3.label: Level 3 near-side piers
sidePiersL3.derivation: Read from the hero photo (earlier reading), measured from the front corner (z 12).

panelWidth.label: Glass panel width
panelWidth.derivation: Read from the hero photo (earlier reading): about 16 glass bays of 4.5-6 ft across the front. Each gap between piers is divided into panels as close to 5.5 ft as fits.

terraceFront.label: Front terrace pavers (extent)
terraceFront.derivation: Read from the hero photo (earlier reading): a stone paver terrace runs along the front, then lawn. 110 x 14 ft centred at (x -8, z 35).

terraceSide.label: Near-side terrace pavers (extent)
terraceSide.derivation: Read from the hero photo (earlier reading): the terrace wraps the near side. 14 x 64 ft centred at (x 55, z 3).

retainingWall.label: Boulder retaining wall at the far left (line, thickness, height)
retainingWall.estimate: The hero photo shows a boulder retaining wall at the far left edge of the lawn (earlier reading); its line, length and size are estimates. Pascal has no boulder kind, so it is a stone-faced wall.

lawn.label: Lawn extent
lawn.estimate: The photo shows lawn beyond the terrace; its extent is not visible and is set large enough to fill every camera view.

invented.label: Back and far-left facades (glass spans in plan coordinates)
invented.estimate: Invented: these facades are not in any published photo. They are mostly stone with a few glass bays so the house reads complete from every side.

wallThickness.label: Exterior wall thickness, levels 1 / 2 / 3
wallThickness.estimate: Ledgestone veneer over a framed wall. Sets how deep the glass sits behind the stone face.

railHeight.label: Glass rail height
railHeight.estimate: 42 in, a common guard height for frameless glass rails; the photo shows rails but their height cannot be measured.

windowHead.label: Stone band above each glass bay
windowHead.estimate: A Pascal window must fit under its wall top, so floor-to-ceiling glass stops 7 cm below the slab soffit. It reads as the head of the frame.

interiors.label: Interior rooms
interiors.value: L1: stair hall, great room, kitchen, guest wing; L2: stair hall, bedrooms, primary suite; L3: stair hall, family room, bunk room
interiors.estimate: Invented: the gallery shows bedrooms, living rooms, a kitchen, a gym and baths, but no plan. One stair hall stacks through all three floors; the remaining rooms are placeholders.

stairs.label: Stairs
stairs.value: two straight flights, 3.6 ft wide, side by side in a 12 ft stair hall at x -6..6, z -26..2
stairs.estimate: Invented: no plan is published. Level 1 to 2 climbs toward the front, level 2 to 3 climbs back.

notes: Two different Aspen houses are published as "Red Mountain". This scene is the Hendrickson Construction house (hendricksoninc.com/our-work/red-mountain). It is NOT CCY Architects' concrete Red Mountain residence: none of CCY's numbers or palette (7,198 SF, board-formed concrete, steel, Swiss Pearl panels, hillside terracing) are used here.
No floor area is published for the Hendrickson house. The gross floor area in the stats above is what this model measures: the outer footprint of each storey, summed.

Wall sconces on the piers (visible in the photo) are not modelled: Pascal's item library has no light fixture, and a scripted object (add_object) needs script compilation, which the in-process build does not enable.

Stone finish: the library stone (flooring-wallstone1) renders orange-brown, too dark for the photo's light warm sandstone. sandstone.jpg is that same library texture, recoloured onto a tan-cream ramp (#b58a5c courses, #d9bf93 to #e2cba2 faces). It is embedded in the scene as the scene material mat_sandstone (a data:image albedo) and painted on every exterior wall face, the terrace edges and both chimneys.
The roof is modelled flat; the photo reads as low-slope (nearly flat), so the pitch is below what the photo can show.
